Revolut alternatives: what to compare in 2026

By the Ibanora teamPublished November 16, 20267 min read

In short

The right Revolut alternative depends on where you live and what you use Revolut for. Euro users can compare N26, bunq and Wise, UK users Monzo and Wise, and businesses Wise Business, bunq Business and Payoneer. Plan fees and protections differ, so check each provider's own pages for your country.

A Revolut alternative is another app or account that covers the part of Revolut you use most: spending in other currencies, holding euros or pounds, sending money abroad, running a business account, or buying crypto. Start from the part you use, then compare providers on that. This guide compares Wise, N26, bunq, Monzo and Payoneer using only each provider's own pricing and legal pages, as of November 2026, with prices for euro and pound users side by side.

Why people look for a Revolut alternative

One reason is cost. Revolut's personal plans in the UK run from Standard, which is free, to Plus at £3.99, Premium at £8.99, Metal at £16.99 and Ultra at £60 a month, according to Revolut's UK pricing page as of November 2026. The UK fee schedule says these plan fees apply to existing customers from December 19, 2026, so an existing plan may cost a different amount until then. As of November 2026, Revolut's German pricing page lists Plus at €2.99, Premium at €8.99, Metal at €15.99 and Ultra at €65 a month.

The free plan has an exchange allowance. As of November 2026, Revolut's UK fee schedule gives Standard customers £1,000 of exchanges a month, with currency, crypto and commodities exchanges counted together, and charges a 1% fair usage fee above that. Revolut's German Standard fee schedule sets the allowance at €1,000 a month, with a 0.5% fee above it, as of November 2026. The German pricing page shows 1% for Standard customers instead, so check the fee in the app before you convert. If you convert more than that every month, a paid plan or a provider that prices each conversion separately may cost less.

Some people want a second account in case one is frozen. The UK Financial Ombudsman Service explains that banks can freeze an account or block payments if they suspect fraud or money laundering, or if a court order requires it, and that they do not have to warn you first. The guidance covers banks in general. A second account at a different firm is one way to keep paying bills while a block is reviewed.

Others want different crypto options, or a business account priced differently. Revolut's UK business fee schedule lists its Basic business plan at £10 a month as of November 2026.

What to check before you switch

  • Status and protection. As of November 2026, N26, bunq and Monzo each list deposit protection on their own pages. Wise says it does not lend out customer money as banks do, and safeguards it instead. Read how each provider describes itself.
  • Currencies and account details. Check which currencies you can hold and whether you get local account details, such as a German or Dutch IBAN, for the currency you are paid in.
  • Plan fee against your use. Add the monthly fee to the conversion and withdrawal fees you would actually pay.
  • Exchange pricing. Some providers convert at the mid-market rate and charge a separate fee. Others use a card network rate. Compare the amount you receive, not the headline.
  • Business needs. If you invoice clients abroad, check receiving fees and annual fees as well as the monthly price.

Revolut alternatives in Europe for euro users

For people in Germany, Austria, Spain and the rest of the euro area, one question to settle first is whether you want a bank account in euros or a multi-currency account.

N26 is a euro bank account. Its plans page lists worldwide card payments as free on all four plans as of November 2026. As of the same date, cash withdrawals outside the eurozone cost 1.7% on Standard and Smart and are free on Go and Metal. The plans page does not say whether you can hold currencies other than euros.

bunq is a Dutch bank. As of November 2026, its page for Germany says you can open an account with a German IBAN, and that Pro and Elite include up to 25 IBANs from the Netherlands, Germany, France, Spain, Belgium, Italy and Ireland. bunq's plans page says Core card payments abroad carry no extra FX fees, as of November 2026.

Wise is an option if you need currencies beyond euros. As of November 2026, its account page says it supports over 40 currencies and uses the mid-market exchange rate, with fees charged when you convert. Wise says it does not lend out customer money as banks do. Its safeguarding page explains that it keeps customer money separate from its own, and that deposit schemes such as the UK's FSCS do not apply in the same way, as of November 2026.

A Revolut alternative in the UK

Monzo is a UK bank. As of November 2026, its help page on fees abroad says you can pay in any currency with a Monzo card without a Monzo fee, at the Mastercard exchange rate. Cash has limits. On the free account, withdrawals outside the EEA are free up to £200 every 30 days as of November 2026, and Monzo charges 3% above your allowance.

Monzo says eligible deposits are covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme up to £120,000 per depositor, as of November 2026, per its FSCS information page. Wise, in the table above, also serves UK users who want to hold several currencies, through Wise Payments Limited.

Revolut Business alternatives

For a Revolut Business alternative, compare the plan fee with what you pay to receive money from abroad and to convert it.

  • Wise Business is free to register and charges a one-time £50 fee to get account details and all Business features, according to its UK business pricing page as of November 2026. The page lists no monthly fee. Conversions cost from 0.24%, depending on the currency.
  • As of November 2026, bunq Business runs from a free plan to Elite at €23.99 a month, per its business plans page. On the same page, Free includes 3 bank accounts, Core 5 and Pro 25.
  • Payoneer's pricing page starts with the fees for receiving money. As of November 2026, its pricing page says receiving into a local-currency receiving account is free, while receiving into a receiving account in a currency other than your local one costs 1% (minimum $1). Moving money between your own Payoneer balances costs 0.50%.

Apps like Revolut for crypto and stablecoins

Revolut offers crypto in its app. As of November 2026, Revolut is migrating crypto customers in the European Economic Area to Revolut Digital Assets Europe Ltd, which it says the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission authorized as a crypto-asset service provider under the EU's MiCA rules. According to Revolut's help page on the migration, customers move by answering questions about their profile and accepting new terms and conditions.

Among the providers above, bunq's plans page says, as of November 2026, that its crypto service is provided by Payward Europe Solutions Limited, trading as Kraken, and warns that crypto trading involves risk of loss. If you mainly want to hold and move stablecoins, look at a dedicated stablecoin wallet and check who provides it and how the provider describes its status.

Where Ibanora fits

Ibanora is a technology brand, not a bank, and it is not regulated in any jurisdiction. It offers multi-currency accounts in EUR, USD, GBP and more, depending on your country and verification, for individuals and businesses, cross-border payments routed through stablecoins, stablecoin and crypto wallets, and on-ramp and off-ramp between ordinary currencies and stablecoins. These services are provided through its partner Mosta Payments Ltd.

If euros are the currency you need most, the euro account page explains how the EUR balance sits next to USD and GBP. Check the product pages for current details before you sign up.

Questions

What is similar to Revolut?

Wise, N26, bunq and Monzo cover similar ground for personal use, and Wise Business, bunq Business and Payoneer for business use. Each covers part of what Revolut does. Wise focuses on holding and converting many currencies, N26 is a euro bank account, bunq offers bank accounts that each have their own IBAN, and Monzo is a UK bank account, per their own pages as of November 2026.

Is there a Revolut alternative with a German IBAN?

bunq says on its page for Germany that you can open an account with a German IBAN, and that its Pro and Elite plans include up to 25 IBANs from the Netherlands, Germany, France, Spain, Belgium, Italy and Ireland, as of November 2026. Check the plans page for the current details before you open an account.

Is my money protected with a Revolut alternative?

It depends on the provider. As of November 2026, N26 lists deposit protection up to €100,000, bunq says deposits are covered by the Dutch Deposit Guarantee Scheme up to €100,000, and Monzo lists FSCS protection for eligible deposits up to £120,000 per depositor. Wise says it does not lend out customer money as banks do, and safeguards it instead.

Does Payoneer charge a monthly fee?

Payoneer's pricing page does not list a monthly fee as of November 2026. It lists an annual account fee of $29.95 that applies only if the account receives less than $6,000 in any 12 consecutive months, and says fees can differ by territory and account type.
